title: Choose the dashboard's visual direction
question: Which direction should shape the redesigned market-intelligence dashboard? Choose a direction or ask for another set.

options.label: The Statistical Atlas
options.lineage: Nineteenth-century statistical atlases and printed data plates
options.thesis: An analytical atlas makes each market series a clear, annotated plate.
options.viewport: A familiar dashboard shell leads with market pulse, then a large chart with a synchronized observation rule and clear data-source notes.
options.risk: The historic reference can feel archival if the typography and interactions are timid.

raised.raise: Keep each claim beside the evidence that supports it, without inheriting the challenger’s neutral-only palette.
Keep instrument lists finite and sortable, without turning market observations into characters.
Make comparison axes and units explicit wherever multiple series or indicators meet.
Show adjustments as numeric deltas with clear units and limits, not as implied forecasts.

options.label: The Market Broadsheet
options.lineage: Financial newspapers’ market tables and editorial data pages
options.thesis: A crisp market desk pairs every headline reading with its history and source.
options.viewport: A deep-green navigation rail anchors a concise market edition: live snapshot first, price history and latest observations side by side.
options.risk: The familiar financial-news reference is effective but conventional by design.

options.label: The Reference-Setting Dashboard
options.lineage: Wide-margin reference editions with a central annotation rail
options.thesis: A shared rail connects every plotted series to its notes and measurements.
options.viewport: The normal dashboard shell stays intact; a central rule marks chart dates and aligns annotations with the chosen instrument.
options.case: Competitive: annotations and measurement context improve clarity, though the editorial source is less native to market users.
options.risk: A narrow central rail can consume chart space or become a layout gimmick.

options.label: The Instrument Network
options.lineage: Metropolitan wayfinding diagrams and route-color systems
options.thesis: Distinct instrument paths stay easy to follow as a shared time-scale view grows.
options.viewport: Standard market controls frame a multiseries price chart; each instrument’s separate path is color-coded and selectable.
options.case: Competitive: strong instrument identification, but route language risks suggesting relationships the data does not establish.
options.risk: A route metaphor can imply causality; series must remain explicitly independent.

options.label: Monochrome Proof Pages
options.lineage: Minimal software product pages with claim-and-proof pairing
options.thesis: A restrained product grid pairs every metric with its evidence.
options.case: Declined: claim-and-proof pairing is useful, but the marketing-page lineage identifies less with daily market analysis and adds no stronger data model.
options.kept: Place each reading beside its source and supporting evidence.
options.risk: The neutral-only treatment can flatten distinctions between market series and statuses.

options.label: The Ranked Roster
options.lineage: Finite collectible catalogs and ranked character rosters
options.thesis: A ranked list makes the selected instruments and segments easy to scan.
options.case: Declined: a ranked roster is clear, but character-goods culture misidentifies a serious market-insight workspace.
options.kept: Keep instrument and segment lists finite, scannable, and sortable.
options.risk: The catalog treatment would make market data feel decorative.

options.label: The Comparison Score
options.lineage: Labanotation’s mirrored columns and duration marks
options.thesis: Paired columns make parallel measurements and time windows explicit.
options.case: Declined: mirrored comparison columns help, but a movement-score grammar does not fit the audience or the market task.
options.kept: Label comparison axes, periods, and units explicitly.
options.risk: The score metaphor can make independent time series appear synchronized.

options.label: The Measured Exposure
options.lineage: Darkroom exposure records and tonal-zone charts
options.thesis: Every adjustment is shown as a measured delta against an explicit baseline.
options.case: Declined: precise deltas help explain scenario controls, but darkroom practice is remote from market users and the visual layers obscure live history.
options.kept: Show scenario adjustments numerically with units, baselines, and caps.
options.risk: Layered overlays could obscure the observed market series.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A conventional market dashboard, executed at full craft.
canonCard.viewport: Market KPIs lead above an interactive price chart, with indicators and segment scenarios in familiar navigation.
canonCard.risk: This polished category pattern is less distinctive by design.
